newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks hit new record for third day in row.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks hit new record for third day in row.

text.p: Swiss shares hit a new record closing high for a third time in a row with the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ending above 5,100 points following a one percent jump.
Dealers said massive foreign buying, Wall Street strength, the U.S. dollar recovery, and technical buying led to the leap.
A flurry of new warrant issues also helped various shares.
Sentiment was seen as bullish. One dealer expected the market to rise until Friday's expiry on the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex).
The SMI ended up 50.1 points, or 0.99 percent, to 5,134.3 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended up 26.81 points to 3,239.68.
Bourse volume was high at 3.03 billion Swiss francs.

Novartis shares led the active list, profiting from Tuesday's news that the pharmaceutical company bought Merck's crop protection unit. Buy recommendation also helped drive Novartis registereds up 30 francs to 2,039, one trader said.
UBS bearers were up 27 francs to 1,466, reportedly buoyed by an upgrade and warrant issues.
Among insurers, Winterthur ended down three francs to 1,128. The company said after the bourse close that net profit 1996 rose by 21 percent.
Dealers said the result was in the upper end of analysts' expectations.
Alusuisse and Holderbank were also lower.
